paper_title: The Non-Uniform Perebor Conjecture for Time-Bounded Kolmogorov Complexity Is False
classifications: Theory of computation → Computational complexity and cryptography
statement: We leave open the question of closing the gap between the lower and upper bounds on the size of black-box Kt -solvers.
context: ▶ Theorem 25. There exists a black-box UTM U b and a constant c such that the following holds for every function t(n) ∈ poly with t(n) ≥ n . For any black-box Kt -solver C = {Cn }n∈N it c U b holds that |Cn | ≥ 2n/2−o(n) for infinitely many n ∈ N. We leave open the question of closing the gap between the lower and upper bounds on the size of black-box Kt -solvers. In the following we give two proofs for the above theorem. In both proofs, we use an universal TM Uoracle with an oracle as our black-box UTM. In the first proof, we we give Uoracle an oracle to a random function, used as a pseudorandom generator (PRG). We then use the Kt -solver to break the PRG. We use the result of Coretti, Dodis, Guo and Steinberger [5] which states that a random function is a good PRG against circuits of size roughly 2n/2 . The second proof, which appears in the full version of this paper, gets slightly worse parameters, but is based on more standard results. In this proof we take the oracle to be a random permutation σ, and use a result from [12] that states of that a random permutation cannot be inverted by a circuit of size 2n/2 . Then, we use Goldreich-Levin hardcore functions to construct a PRG from σ.
